A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we established in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of multiple neurons in the spinal dorsal horns by introducing a FRET-based calcium indicator, Yellow Cameleon 3.60 into the neurons by in uterine electroporation, and that this method enabled us to visualize the three dimensional distribution of sensory stimulation evoked neuronal activity in vivo.

we have established in vivo calcium imaged-based analysis of neuronal activity of spinal dorsal horn neurons and revealed the three-dimensional distribution of sensory stimulation-induced neuronal activity in the mouse spinal cord.

we established in vivo imaging of sensory stimulation-evolved neuronal activities of spinal dorsal horn neurons and found that the distribution of these neuronal activities is consistent with that of primary aferent fibers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in vivo calcium imaging can be used to monitor neuronal activity of spinal dorsal horn neurons in response to naturalistic cutaneous sensory stimulation in freely moving animals.
we have demonstrated that in utero electoporation can be used to label neurons with genetically encoded calcium indicators, and that these can be imaged in vivo using two-photon microscopy.
the laminar distribution of the neuronal activity of spinal dorsal horn neurons in the spinal dorsal column is largely in agreement with the distribution of primary afferents.
